standing: PROVED — THE TROUBLE LANE, and THE TROUBLE TICKET IS THE DAMPER. Akien's two statements built this: nothing fails silently, everything that can't escalate elsewhere fails to trouble tickets; AND a system alarm is raised once, its count increments, because demanding attention that has already been demanded is not productive. The second closed the chatter question that hysteresis could only have TUNED: identity-plus-count needs no width, because the scarce thing is ATTENTION and attention is spent in full when the first ticket lands. Fifty flaps = one ticket that says 50. Truth is never damped (exact count, moving timestamps, bounded occurrence tail); only NOTIFICATION is. Only the recipient clears, only by naming what changed; a fault returning after a clear is a NEW ticket at count 1 carrying the fix that did not hold. Records are git-JSON in CairnCommons/troubles/. Normal operating state = live() EMPTY, and the device says so in its own state().

note: THIS END IS THE HOLDER. The shim's drain generalised from one lane to three (GATES = raise, clear, reconcile) with a PER-GATE watermark, because the marks are filename high-water marks and 'c' < 'r' — one shared mark silently skips a clear that shares a stamp with a raise. _fold dispatches by gate and RAISES on an unknown one rather than returning, because a drain that scanned a lane it cannot apply would drop the emission silently. The clear fold DECLINES a not-live identity instead of refusing it: a refusal HOLDS the watermark by design (a fault must not be skipped past), so a declined clear taking the refusal path would wedge the lane forever. Reconcile clears only identities under its scope prefix — another reporter's trouble in the same store is untouchable. Five teeth added, all three properties mutation-tested at 34/35 with only the intended tooth red. || THE FINDING THIS VOYAGE OWES A READER IN A YEAR: A BUS DIAL IS A DATABASE DIAL, STATICALLY. cairn/tools/base/bus_client.py reaches denied capability two ways — inference_seam() imports cairn.devices.inference_domain, and _wire() imports bus.bus which imports cairn.devices.db_domain — and build_inspector's own fire_path_unreachable sieve walks the STATIC import graph counting function-local imports as edges, so laziness cannot evade it. Therefore any in-process bus dial statically reaches a database and the inference host, and the build inspector, which must reach neither, CAN NEVER BE A BUS CLIENT. Commit 433cdc9 shipped the chart's 'reconcile clears via the verb' bound and the sieve red it; the bound was not awkward, it was impossible. THE REPLACEMENT IS THE SEAM THE RAISE ALREADY CROSSES: two more emission lanes beside raise_trouble — clear_trouble(identity, by, what_changed) and reconcile_troubles(scope, still, by, what_changed) — each with its own gate name and therefore its own watermark in the drain. Sending is a tool; holding is owned. 433cdc9's ownership reasoning was RIGHT and its conclusion did not follow: what must happen in the owner's hand is the DECIDING and the WRITING, not the ASKING. reconcile is the shape that made it work — a reconciler cannot know what is STALE without READING the store, and both read routes are shut, so it hands the holder the COMPLETE current picture under a scope and the holder clears the rest, moving both halves of the read-modify-write into the one process that owns the JSON.
